# 2.11.10

Date: 2026-09-21
Tag: 2.11.10

## Overview

2.x is the old stable release series. Users are encouraged to update to the
latest 3.x release.

This is a bugfix release. It resolves 15 issues since the previous version.

Please consider the full list of user-visible changes below.

## Compatibility

Tarantool 2.x and 3.x are compatible in the binary data layout, client-server
protocol, and replication protocol. It means upgrade may be performed with zero
downtime for read requests

Agentic: Chat Completions tool calls send vendor fields back (Gemini 3 thought signatures, #296). Flow: escalate_model runs code repairs on a stronger model. See docs/CHANGELOG.md.
Worker state dir binds per run, not through a process-wide env var. Opt-in in-process map walks. See docs/CHANGELOG.md.

**Opt-in: one shared Codex host for a flow walk.** A Codex worker starts its
own `codex exec` process: the launcher, the native binary, a login-shell
snapshot and git probes. Native Codex runs its subagents as threads in one
process. Codex lab R200 measured about 114 s from `codex exec` launch to the
first model turn for each cold builder, because the lab guards every process.
R202 measured 0.05 s from a native subagent spawn to its own turn.

- Set `"defaults": {"codex_host": true}` in the graph, or
  `PUP

**A nested builder's `revise` no longer blocks follow-up reuse.** Codex R196
(PM 1.46.1, one builder per region inside each group, map `reuse` on): the
follow-up named regions in groups 01 and 03 only. Groups 00 and 02 did not
reuse ("its item graph reads the request"), so 8 extra region builders ran.

- `_reads_request` removed `revise` only from the entry node itself. When the
  entry is a map, the inner builder's `revise` (with `{{prev}}`) stayed in
  the searched text, and the item counted as one that r

**A map inside a map item knows the outer items' writers.** R179 replica,
one builder per region inside each of the four groups: a region builder in
group_00 wrote only its own files, but its write-scope gate charged it with
79 render files from builders in the other groups. Its item failed although
the builder passed.

- An outer item's scope now includes what the items of its own inner maps
  write (`_item_scopes`). The outer map's disjoint check covers them too.
- A nested map gives its items the outer p

write sandbox, and `--disable memories --disable multi_agent`.
the ChangeTime of `state.sqlite3` moved, but its size and LastWriteTime did

**A map item's builder owns only its own verdict.** In the Codex R163 study
(PM 1.45.0, reuse on, follow-up), the group_03 builder ran the world check
while the group_01 builder still worked. The check failed only in group_01's
regions, the builder ended FAIL, and that FAIL failed the item although its
own fresh review passed. The run stopped at the map before the new world
review.

- **Item frame.** A build agent inside a map item now learns its item key,
  that the map waits for every item before later st

**A follow-up can keep unchanged map items.** In the Codex R157 cohort (PM
1.44.0, N16 grouped, `gpt-6.1-sol` high), every follow-up rebuilt and
reviewed all four groups. The request named only the revised regions, so the
unchanged groups spent build and review time on revalidation. In one
repetition an unchanged group held the map finish at 202 s.

- **Opt-in `reuse` on a map.** `reuse: {"inputs": ..., "names": ...}`. The
  map records a fingerprint of each finished item: its task (item graph and
  item va

**Flows send less work through each repair.** In the Codex R138 cohort
(1.43.4), PM took 2.38 times the native work time. A local replica of that
graph (16 regions in 4 groups, `gpt-6.1-sol` high) showed where the time
went. Three of four group reviews failed on their first visit. Each repair
re-sent the full build contract, so the builder started the task again. The
world review read all 144 views again after 16 current unit reviews.

- **Gate preview.** A build agent sees the shell commands and judge task

**A judge binds its review to its own `files`.** In the Codex R138 cohort
(1.43.4), the world judge after a map of group builds declared
`files: ["regions/*.py"]`. Its root result had no `reviewed` digest, count or
scope. The review scope came only from code agents in the judge's own graph,
and the root graph has a map, a shell and a judge, but no code agent. The
group judges inside the map items had digests. The world judge did not.

- A judge's review scope is now its own rendered `files` plus the `files`

Updates now keep Tidesight's code private.

- **The update keeps the permissions of the code it replaces.** If `app/` is closed to other accounts (the deployment guide's `chmod 700 app`), every folder and file of the new code is too, and so is the download while it is checked. The copies refreshed in the website's folder get the modes the web server needs (`tidesight.fcgi` 755, `.htaccess` 644).
- **Installations updated by 0.2.0's or 0.1.0's updater are repaired** by the next cron run after this update, on
- **Collector:** Python's standard library, every hit appended raw to SQLite; FastCGI or CGI on shared hosting, with PHP, Node and Cloudflare Workers connectors that pass the same conformance suite.
